sections.title: SB 003 — Operations Update from Mark Redd · 2025-01-13
sections.text:
Reference # CPKCSB-03-25 
  Posted Date / Time: ____/____/25 – ________ 
 
SYSTEM BULLETIN 
 
To: All Operations Employees All Regions  Date: January 13, 2025 
 
SUBJECT:  Operations Update from Mark Redd 
 
 
Welcome to 2025!  
 
I hope your holidays were safe and happy. Thank you to the many railroaders who worked over 
the holidays to keep our trains moving safely and efficiently. When I reflect on 2024, I think of 
how much we accomplished and all the challenges we overcame together during our first full 
year as CPKC. We have a unique and exciting story to write together, and I look forward to 
what’s to come in 2025 as we continue our CPKC journey. 
 
The new year arrived with intense winter weather across parts of the network, with seven U.S. 
states including Missouri declaring emergencies last week. The Midwest experienced freezing 
rain and heavy snow that impacted railroaders who live and operate in the area. Thank you to 
the many railroaders who worked hard during and after the storm to help our operations recover 
from its effects.  
 
Make sure you read the seasonal bulletins that highlight ways we can all look out for each other 
and stay safe in winter conditions. They are posted in the safety section on CPKC Station. You 
can also find helpful tips for driving in winter weather there. I encourage you to take a moment to 
read this important information.  
 
Holiday Train and Holiday Express make a difference across North America 
 
CPKC’s Holiday Train program completed another successful tour just before the holidays, 
raising more than $1.75 million and collecting 130,000 pounds of food for neighbours in need. 
Over 345,000 people are estimated to have attended a Holiday Train show in Canada and the 
U.S., and countless people experienced the joy of seeing the train pass through their 
communities. Thank you to the many railroaders who played a role in another safe and 
successful Holiday Train season, and to those who supported the Holiday Express in its efforts 
to raise $108,000 and spread holiday cheer and Tren Navideño as it once again brightened the 
season for community members in Mexico. These programs have a significant impact on so 
many people, and they simply would not exist without the hard work of the railroaders who plan 
and safely execute them year after year.  
 
Going Home Safe in 2025 
 
The new year presents a fresh opportunity to start the first minute of every day with a 
commitment to going Home Safe. I ask you to keep safety at the forefront of every job, every 
action and everything you do. Let’s start the year with a renewed commitment to looking out for 
each other and going Home Safe.
Reference # CPKCSB-03-25 
I wish you a safe, happy and healthy New Year! 
 
 
Mark Redd 
Executive Vice-President and Chief Operating Officer 
 
 
 
 
 
Home Safe is a commitment to be vigilant about personal safety and the safety of co-workers.

To: All Employees  US Date: January 23, 2025 
 
 
SUBJECT: Update to Physical Wellness Subsidy Claim Submission Deadline 
 
CPKC values a healthy workforce and encourages active lifestyles by offering a Physical Wellness 
Subsidy. This subsidy reimburses 50% of eligible fitness -related expenses, up to $600 per 
calendar year.  Starting January 2024, the deadline for submitting expenses was changed to  
December 31 each year. We understand not all employees may have received this information.  
As a result, the deadline for submitting 2024 expenses has been extended to February 28, 2025.   
 
On a go forward basis the deadline for subsidy submission will be : February 28, of each 
year.   
 
Eligible expenses include: 
• Membership dues or fees, for employees only, at licensed fitness facilities for classes such 
as: gym memberships, squash, running tracks, fitness classes, yoga, pilates, martial arts, 
aqua fitness, and swimming. 
• Fees for employee online subscriptions to instructor -led virtual fitness classes.  (New 
benefit in 2024) 
 
Fees for recreational activities (i.e., golf, hockey etc.) and sporting equipment are not eligible for 
reimbursement.  
 
To submit your expenses under the Physical Wellness Subsidy, please send proof of payment 
along with a completed application form to employee_services@cpkcr.com.  Claims previously 
declined, for 2024, due to a missed deadline will be reprocessed.  Please resubmit to 
employee_services@cpkcr.com.   
 
If you require a copy of an application form or have any questions regarding this program, please 
reference the policy on CPKC statio n > Policies > Physical Wellness  or contact  
Benteam@cpkcr.com .

sections.title: SB 005 — Operations update: A message from Mark Redd · 2025-01-27
sections.text:
Reference # CPKCSB-005-25                                    Posted Date/Time _____/_____/_____-________ 
 
SYSTEM BULLETIN 
 
To: All Employees  US Date: January 27, 2025 
 
 
SUBJECT: Operations update: A message from Mark Redd  
 
January has delivered intense winter weather across many parts of the network. We’ve seen winter 
storms in the Houston area, heavy snow in Kansas City and significant extreme cold, wind and snow 
across the Upper Midwest, Northeast and most of Canada.  
 
I want to thank all of you who keep the railroad moving through these blasts of winter. Whether you work 
to keep tracks safe and switches clean, operate trains or perform other work that keeps our railroad 
operating safely in harsh conditions, your work makes a difference. It takes a lot of grit to be out in the 
cold, snow and wind maintaining the network and running trains. Please keep watching out for each 
other and if you see something, say something and get home safely.  
 
2025 CEO Awards for Excellence winners 
 
The 2025 CEO Awards for Excellence winners have been announced, and they showcase outstanding 
work in a variety of areas. These awards recognize CPKC railroaders who go above and beyond in the 
areas that are foundational to our business: Operate Safely, Provide Service, Develop People, Optimize 
Assets and Control Costs. Each year we also celebrate our Community Hero and Terminal of the Year.  
 
From the crew that delivered the Final Spike Steam Tour to the railroaders leading the charge on 
improving fuel efficiency to the team that made trailblazing moves to strengthen our pensions, there are 
many great examples of CPKC railroaders who are working together and delivering outstanding results. 
Our Community Heroes looked danger in the eye and saved lives. And the whole team at San Luis 
Potosí earned the Terminal of the Year award for their efficiency, teamwork and commitment to going 
Home Safe. 
 
See the names of all the winners by reading Mr. Creel’s message on CPKC Station and CPKC XChange. 
If you know a winner, congratulate them! Watch for the next issue of Connect magazine this spring and 
read more about why these railroaders are being recognized for their excellence.  
 
Values and Foundations | Precision scheduled railroading (PSR) the CPKC way 
 
The new year provides not only an opportunity to recommit to going Home Safe, but also an opportunity 
to step back and refocus on living our values and foundations in all that we do.  
 
Our foundations are what we do – PSR done the right way. Our values are how we do it. And everything 
we do is built on a foundation of respect. 
 
PSR is a culture of excellence and safety that we embrace 24/7, 365 days a year. It is a fundamental 
focus on service, asset utilization, controlling costs, developing our people and investing in safety to run 
a safer railway. Please take a few minutes and recommit to understanding our values and foundations 
and living them in your work every day.  
 
Stay healthy and stay safe, 
 
Mark Redd 
Executive Vice-President and Chief Operating Officer 
Work Smart, Stay Safe

sections.title: SB 006 — A message from the President & CEO: CPKC delivers strong fourth quarter · 2025-01-29
sections.text:
Reference # CPKCSB-006-25                                    Posted Date/Time _____/_____/_____-________ 
 
SYSTEM BULLETIN 
 
To: All Employees  US Date: January 29, 2025 
 
 
SUBJECT: A message from the President & CEO: CPKC delivers strong fourth quarter 
and full-year results. 
 
Fellow railroaders, 
 
Today, we announced CPKC’s fourth quarter and full year 2024 results which demonstrate your hard work 
and dedication to finishing our first full year as CPKC strong. In Q4, we grew volume and improved our 
safety performance allowing us to deliver industry-leading earnings growth for the year in 2024. With this 
strong finish, we are ready to continue growing in 2025.  
 
During the fourth quarter, we achieved revenues of $3.9 billion, an increase of 3 percent compared to Q4 
2023. Volumes, as measured by Revenue Ton Miles (RTMs), increased 2 percent. Our reported operating 
ratio (OR) decreased to 59.7 percent from 61.8 perc ent in Q4 2023 and core adjusted combined OR 
improved to 57.1 percent from 58.7 percent in Q4 2023, a tremendous result. Reported operating income 
reached $1.6 billion for the quarter. This led to reported diluted earnings per share (EPS) of $1.28 and 
core adjusted combined diluted EPS of $1.29, an increase of 9 percent. In Q4, Federal Railroad 
Administration (FRA)-reportable personal injury frequency decreased to 0.84 from 1.13 in Q4 2023 and 
FRA-reportable train accident frequency decreased to 1.03 from 1.08 in Q4 2023.  
 
From a full-year 2024 perspective, we achieved 3 percent RTM growth, which is a testament to the strength 
of our railroaders and the power of this new network. In 2024, FRA -reportable personal injury frequency 
decreased to 0.95 from 1.15 in 2023, but FRA -reportable train accident frequency increased slightly to 
1.01 from 0.99 in 2023.  
 
For more on the results, please see today’s press release at cpkcr.com.  
 
Q4 milestones 
 
• Construction was completed on the new international railroad bridge span over the Rio Grande 
from Laredo, Texas, to Nuevo Laredo, Tamaulipas. The rail bridge will now be known as the Patrick 
J. Ottensmeyer International Railway Bridge in honor of Pat whose  leadership and vision were 
instrumental in the development and completion of this important project.   
• The Surface Transportation Board approved CSX’s and CPKC’s respective applications regarding 
acquisition of the rail lines operated by G&W’s Meridian & Bigbee Railroad. On Dec. 1, the first 
CPKC train traveled the new subdivision after interchanging with CSX.  
• Our Holiday Train program completed another successful year, raising more than $1.75 million and 
collecting 130,000 pounds of food to help people struggling with food insecurity. The Holiday 
Express raised $108,000 for local food banks and Tren Navideño once again brightened the season 
for community members in Mexico. 
• Exceptional railroaders from across the continent gathered in Calgary in October to celebrate the 
6th annual CPKC Safety Awards for Excellence. The gala brought together 28 safety leaders and 
family members from across our North American network to celebrate their achievements and 
reinforce why safety matters and how we can all help each other go home safely.
Reference # CPKCSB-006-25                                    Posted Date/Time _____/_____/_____-________ 
 
Safety 
 
In 2024, for the second consecutive year, CPKC led the industry with the lowest FRA -reportable train 
accident frequency among Class 1 railroads, building on Canadian Pacific's legacy of 17 consecutive years 
of industry leadership. Together, we are doing what we said we would do, bringing a new standard of 
safety to the North American rail landscape.  
 
Our journey to operate safely is one that has no end. Every day, every minute, every second we must be 
thinking about safety, looking out for each other and doing all we can to go Home Safe. Whether you work 
on the ballast or in an office, you play a role in our safety journey.  
 
As we move into a new year, I ask that you keep safety top of mind in all that you do. Watch out for your 
fellow railroaders and approach each day, each job with a beginner’s mind when it comes to safety. 
Together, we can do better today than we did yesterday.  
 
I am truly humbled to be railroading with you and look forward to achieving great things together in 2025.  
 
Respectfully, 
 
 
Keith Creel 
President and CEO 
 
 
Work Smart, Stay Safe

sections.text:
Reference # CPKCSB-009-25                                    Posted Date/Time _____/_____/_____-________ 
 
SYSTEM BULLETIN 
 
To: All T&E Employees  All US Regions Date: February 6, 2025 
 
 
SUBJECT: CPKC Public Safety Communications Center – 1-800-716-9132 
 
CPKC is committed to providing a safe work environment. As employees, you are our eyes and ears on 
the ground and across the network. We count on you to keep a watchful eye during your day-to-day 
work. Because you can distinguish between suspicious activity and your everyday routine, we encourage 
you to be alert. If something does not look or feel right, report it. 
 
CPKC Police is aware of recent media reports covering incidents of cargo theft from freight trains in 
southwestern U.S. states, away from CPKC’s network. Employees play a critical role in CPKC’s 
dedication to operating safely and can continue to do their part in protecting themselves and others by 
reporting suspicious items, persons, or activity. The below tactics have been associated with recently 
reported cargo thefts: 
 
• Individuals have attempted to access intermodal facilities to plant GPS trackers on containers and 
attempted to target high value cargo based on the presence of high-security locks. 
• Individuals have attempted to elicit sensitive corporate information on topics including freight 
manifests or train schedules. 
• Individuals have approached moving trains and cut air hoses or attempted to turn angle cocks, 
which causes trains to go into emergency and stop. 
• Individuals have unloaded goods from containers and either loaded them into nearby vehicles or 
stashed them for pick up at a later date.  
• Indicators of possible cargo thefts include: 
o Convoys of unknown vehicles pacing or approaching trains in remote areas; 
o Cargo vans being parked alongside ROWs in remote areas; and 
o Unknown persons being observed boarding trains following a loss of air.  
 
If you observe a suspicious individuals or activities on CPKC property, or in proximity to rail operations, 
you should: 
 
• Contact the CPKC Public Safety Communication Centre (PSCC) at toll-free 1-800-716-9132 
from any Canadian or U.S. location, or the emergency line in Mexico at 011-52-81-8305-
7911.  
• Do not attempt to investigate or photograph suspicious activities and report those to the 
PSCC.   
• By reporting suspicious activities, CPKC employees can play a central role in ensuring the 
safety of our employees and operations, and the communities in which we operate. 
 
CPKC Police closely monitors events to assess risks to our company.  With your collaboration, our 
awareness and ability to assess risks can be multiplied many times over. Safety is our collective 
responsibility, so it is important for CPKC employees to remain vigilant and aware of the potential for 
suspicious activity on our property. 
 
If you see something, please say something! 
CPKC Police 24hr Public Safety Communications Center 1-800-716-9132 
 
Work Smart, Stay Safe

Reference # CPKCSB-010-25                                    Posted Date/Time _____/_____/_____-________ 
 
SYSTEM BULLETIN 
 
To: All Employees  US Date: February 10, 2025 
 
 
SUBJECT: Operations update: A message from Mark Redd. 
 
 
Consequence Leadership (CL) provides the foundation for leading the CPKC way. It is a positive, practical, 
proven set of tools and way of thinking that truly sets us apart from other railroads and other companies. 
CL is about Q4 leadership, holding ourselves and others accountable, creating an environment of respect 
and using the tools to positively impact people to achieve world-class results.  
  
I recently sat down with Maeghan Albiston, Senior Vice-President and Chief Human Resources Officer, to 
talk about what CL is, what makes it unique and share insights into our leadership journeys.  
  
I encourage you to watch the video on CPKC Station and consider your own leadership journey.  
  
Whether you lead people or lead by example, you make an impact! 
  
Leadership Legacy Committee (LLC): Purpose and new members 
  
The LLC, founded in 2021, is a working group of senior leaders whose mission is to help develop tough 
and inspiring Q4 leaders - leaders who leave our railroad better than they found it. Through understanding 
and practicing Consequence Leadership every day and on every job, we strengthen ourselves, our teams 
and our railroad. I would like to welcome two new members to the LLC: Nick Walker, Senior Vice-President 
Operations East and Brad Robertson, Vice -President Mechanical Car. I would also like to thank two  
departing members, Tracy Miller, Senior Vice-President Operations South and Baden Tidd, Vice-President 
Mechanical Locomotive, who were an integral part of building the LLC into what it is today. Thank you, 
Tracy and Baden, for your dedication to developing people.  
  
Official dedication of Patrick J. Ottensmeyer International Railway Bridge 
  
On Feb. 6, CPKC celebrated the official dedication of the Patrick J. Ottensmeyer International Railway 
Bridge. This bridge and the man whose work made it possible both represent vision, connection and 
legacy. Completion of the additional span more than dou bles our capacity to move freight through the 
border at Laredo, the largest international trade port of entry in North America. Pat’s vision and leadership 
played a big role in the development and completion of this project, and it was especially moving to  have 
his fiancée Deanne, and three daughters join us for the dedication ceremony. Thank you to everyone 
whose work helped make this project a tremendous success.  
  
 
Stay healthy and stay safe, 
  
 
 Mark Redd 
Executive Vice-President and Chief Operating Officer 
 
 
 
Work Smart, Stay Safe

sections.text:
Reference # CPKCSB-012-25                                    Posted Date/Time _____/_____/_____-________ 
 
SYSTEM BULLETIN 
 
To: All Employees  US Date: February 24, 2025 
 
 
SUBJECT: Operations update: A message from Mark Redd. 
 
It’s often said that railroading is an outdoor sport, and railroaders in Western Canada and the Prairies have 
once again been challenged to safely deliver in prolonged extreme winter conditions as these regions dealt with 
extreme cold and snow. Temperatures plunged to the -50s in some parts of the Prairies last weekend, prompting 
extreme cold warnings. While these warnings encouraged people to stay indoors, our railroaders were out in 
the elements maintaining track and working to keep trains moving.  
  
Bitter temperatures also gripped the operation across the U.S. Midwest for many days and nights during this 
February cold snap, and in the last week, historic amounts of snowfall blanketed eastern Canada. Winter comes 
every year, and no one has more experience at winter railroading than us, but that doesn’t make it any easier.     
  
Thank you to everyone who kept trains running safely and efficiently, including those from other operating 
departments, various Train & Engine regions and the Calgary head office who jumped in to support the 
operations in Moose Jaw, Regina and throughout S askatchewan during the cold snap. There has been a 
magnitude of railroaders from many departments helping wherever they can, and that help made an impact.  
  
Canadian labour update

beautiful new space for railroaders to work every day. The new space brings the Monterrey OC in line with other 
state-of-the-art OC’s across CPKC’s network and features a training center supporting 120 employees in-person 
and offering the option for remote training sessions. The training center recently hosted the first Consequence 
Leadership session of 2025.  
  
As with other new OCs on the network, the Monterrey OC pays tribute to the great history of the two railroads 
that came together to form CPKC. The OC features a model railway exhibition, displaying historical model trains 
as a reminder of our past and the great future we share.

I recently sat down with Maeghan Albiston, Senior Vice-President and Chief Human Resources Officer, to talk

To: All Employees  US Date: March 24, 2025 
 
SUBJECT: Operations update: A message from Mark Redd. 
 
Maintaining track is a demanding job in the best weather conditions; safely maintaining track in the extreme weather 
that Saskatchewan presents requires next level grit and commitment. For 36 years, Brett Reynolds, Track 
Maintenance Foreman, has been doing just that, braving biting cold, snow, bitter winds and hot summers on the 
Maple Creek Subdivision to keep tracks safe.  
  
Brett is a dedicated, impactful railroader and leader, and our 2025 Railroader of the Year. Please join me in 
congratulating Brett and thanking him for his many years of exemplary service!  
  
To read and see more about Brett and why he won, visit CPKC Station  or CPKC XChange. And watch out for the 
next issue of Connect magazine this spring to read about Brett and other outstanding awarding-winning railroaders.   
 
First safety walkabout of 2025 
On March 18, we held our first network -wide safety walkabout of the year. The theme for this walkabout was 
accountability as individuals and leaders, and how that applies to safety. Acting safely isn’t an option. It isn’t something 
we do just because regulators are on site. We must do our jobs safely. That is our accountability. Regulators are 
there to support and oversee, but it is our responsibility to do what’s right and help each other go home safely every 
day. There were many excellent engagements during the walkabout and participants shared some great exampl es 
of what they learned.  Check out the recap story on CPKC Station and CPKC Xchange for more.  
 
Labour Relations 
In Canada, the United Steelworkers (USW) became the third union this year to successfully ratify a four-year collective 
agreement renewal with CPKC covering 2025 -2028. The TCRC -MWED and Unifor also ratified their agreements 
earlier this year. All three CPKC agreements provide for wage increases of 3 percent in each year of a four-year deal, 
along with benefit improvements for employees working in the Mechanical, Engineering, Clerical and Intermodal 
departments. These improvements reflect patterns realized w ith other Canadian railways. Outstanding agreements 
governing the TCRC (T&E and RCTC) will be heard before Mediator/Arbitrator William Kaplan starting April 7, 2025. 
I will share further developments as they arise.  
 
Stay aware, stay safe: Spring hazards 
The arrival of spring is a welcome sign that we are through the worst of winter’s cold and snow, but spring also brings 
changing weather conditions that impact our operations. The spring freeze/thaw cycle and rain can create hazards 
such as ice, flooding and washouts, sinkholes, debris and more. Track maintenance teams are inspecting track and 
ballast, and we all play a role in railroading safely as we move into spring. Please protect against slips, trips and falls 
by clearing debris and spills and clearing or sanding snow and ice. Stay aware, report hazards immediately and let’s 
all go Home Safe.  
 
Day N: Preparing for change on May 3 
As we get closer to May 3, known as Day N, it is crucial that railroaders who will experience change learn how to 
work in CPKC applications. If you received an email invitation to complete the People Station pre-work training videos 
prior to attending in -person training, I ask that you complete that training. For union employees, assigned People 
Station training courses must be completed by April 15.   
  
The courses can be completed at the kiosks before going off duty. Employees with an iPad must register their iPads 
and then complete the AIR 2.0 and Switch & Build simulator training.

Stay healthy and stay safe, 
 
Mark Redd 
Executive Vice-President and Chief Operating Officer

Reference # CPKCSB-016-25                                    Posted Date/Time _____/_____/_____-________ 
 
SYSTEM BULLETIN 
 
To: T&E Employees  US Date: March 31, 2025 
 
 
SUBJECT: Letter from the FRA on  Personal Electronic Devices 
 
CPKC along with all of the other Class 1 railroads in the US have received the following message from 
the FRA on the use of personal electronic devices: 
 
All, 
We are faced with a persistent, and frankly, escalating problem: the unauthorized use of personal 
electronic devices within restricted operational environments. The introduction of the smartwatch has only 
exacerbated this issue, creating a new avenue for non-compliance. 
  
It is my assessment that some officers and employees either fail to comprehend the gravity of this issue 
or misunderstand the scope of the restrictions. In certain instances, violations appear to result from a 
deliberate decision to disregard established rules and regulations. 
  
My objective is not to engage in a punitive exercise, cataloging infractions and escalating enforcement 
measures. Rather, I seek to provide an opportunity to inform you directly of what we are observing, and to 
emphasize to industry that compliance is both necessary and achievable. 
  
I have engaged with labor representatives to ensure a shared understanding. 
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 
CPKC is determined to be the safest railway in the industry, and this cannot happen without 100% rules 
compliance. We are sending out this System Bulletin in order to bring the awareness to GCOR 2.21 
Electronic Device rule which is an ongoing issue across the country. Operating Rules and Practices will 
be increasing the focus on the use of electronic devices while performing compliance audits. 
 
Please refresh yourself with GCOR 2.21 Electronic Device to make sure you are doing your part to make 
CPKC the safest railway in the industry. 
 
GCOR 2.21 Electronic Devices (Including update from System Special Instructions) 
This rule outlines the requirements for use of electronic devices. As used in this rule, the following  
definitions apply: 
 
Electronic Device.  An electronic or electrical device used to conduct oral, written, or visual 
communication; place or receive a telephone call; send or read an electronic mail message or text 
message; look at pictures; read a book or other written material; play a game; na vigate the Internet; 
navigate the physical world; play, view, or listen to a video; play, view or listen to a television broadcast; 
play or listen to music; execute a computational function; or, perform any other function that is not 
necessary for the health or safety of the person and that entails the risk of distracting the employee or 
another employee from a safety related task.
Reference # CPKCSB-016-25                                    Posted Date/Time _____/_____/_____-________ 
 
Railroad Operating Employee. An individual who is: 
• Engaged in or connected with the movement of a train including a hostler, 
• A train employee providing commuter or intercity rail passenger transportation, 
or 
• Subject to hours-of-service governing train service employees. 
 
The use of any electronic device is prohibited if that use would interfere with an employee’s performance 
of safety-related duties. 
 
A. Personal or Railroad Supplied Electronic Devices 
Personal or railroad supplied electronic devices may be used as necessary: 
• To respond to an emergency situation involving the operation of the railroad,  
• To respond to an emergency encountered while on duty, 
• As a communication device in the event of radio malfunction. 
 
B.  Personal Electronic Devices Changed to read as follows:  
Personal electronic devices are prohibited and must be turned off, stored out of sight and not on your 
ALSO person with any earpieces removed from the ear. Not applicable to medical devices.  
 
Exceptions:  
Personal cellular devices may be used in the case of an emergency or during radio failure for voice 
communication only. Employee may use personal cellular devices (for voice communication only):  
When deadheading in other than a locomotive.  
During a recognized break or meal period provided that they are:  
• Not in a locomotive.  
• Not in a piece of on-track equipment.  
• Not foul of any track.  
All other forms of personal electronic devices are always prohibited while on duty. Cell phone must be 
turned off and stowed (not on person) when voice call has been completed.  
 
Employees are prohibited from using a digital storage and display function of an electronic device to refer 
to a railroad rule, special instruction, timetable, or other directive.  
   
Use of a personal standalone camera to take a photograph is prohibited.  
 
Foreign line railroads operating over CP railroad may use an electronic device to refer to a railroad rule, 
special instruction, timetable, or other directive as allowed by their railroad operating rules. When not in 
use it must be turned off and stowed.    
 
A personal stand-alone calculator, digital watch whose only purpose is as a timepiece and medical devices 
that are consistent with the railroad’s standards may be used as necessary in the performance of duties.  
 
C. Railroad Authorized Electronic Devices   
Railroad authorized electronic devices may be used outside of the cab of a locomotive when:  
Employee on the ground using the device is not foul of the track and all crew members, agree that it is 
safe to use the device.  
 
Work Smart, Stay Safe

SYSTEM BULLETIN 
 
To: All Employees  US Date: April 16, 2025 
 
SUBJECT: 2025 Spring/Summer Preparedness – Hazard Awareness 
 
To prepare for seasonal changes, please discuss the common hazards you may face in your workplace, their impacts, 
and what mitigations can be put in place to reduce risk as we head into spring and  summer.  
 Before beginning work:   
• Stretch and warm up the body. The muscles you will use for the day must be ready for work.   
• Inspect PPE before using it and ensure you have all appropriate PPE with you.   
• Check the weather and dress appropriately for the task. Have the proper clothing and other necessities 
to be better prepared to work in any environment.   
• Drink plenty of water to stay hydrated. Hydration starts the day before.  
• Take the time to develop a work plan. Don’t rush the process. It is a critical step in ensuring that you   
and your co-workers stay safe and go home safe.   
 
Reporting incidents and safety hazards helps us all understand the safety challenges we face in our workplace 
and how we can learn from others.   
Last year, when seasons change, the safety hazards below were reported from April to June. Take a moment to 
review and recognize how they impacted our workplaces in different ways, which can lead to  sprains, strains, or 
other types of injuries:   
• While detraining a stationary cut of cars, the boot heel sunk into a hole beside the rail.   
• A sinkhole was spotted beside an old cement footing.   
• Potholes, mud on a track, and drainage on the roadways.   
• Melting snow has revealed debris and other trip hazards in a yard.   
• Rail has a section of ties that have sunk due to thawing and freezing.   
• The branches of trees are close to a track. Other parts of trees have been rubbed by trains and are   
broken with protruding branches. This could cause injury to an employee riding equipment.   
• Weeds are concealing holes and other tripping hazards.      
 
Keep these quick tips in mind when working this spring and summer:  
• Hydrate, Hydrate, Hydrate. Proper hydration is crucial when working in hot environments. 
• Report any vegetation hazards (i.e., crossing/signal sightlines, brush, and weed issues).     
• Report poor condition/missing signage (i.e., faded/weathered close/restricted clearance and derail 
signs, blue/red flags, etc.).  
• Increase stinging and biting insect awareness should be heightened. Please use insect spray and tags 
in locations where these insects make homes.  
• Report any hard-to-throw derails and switches. Do not overexert yourself. Ask for assistance if  
required.  
• Inspect derails and low frequency used switches with caution for potential stinging insect homes and 
snakes.    
• Report high water or spring run-off damage and/or washouts.    
• Be aware of the weather and seek shelter if violent weather poses an immediate threat (i.e.,  
lightning, increased tornado risk, etc.).     
 
For more information, speak to your supervisor and / or refer to our Spring / Summer Hazards Awareness package 
posted in your workplace and on CPKC Station: Operations – Safety – Seasonal Bulletins or type keyword <seasonal 
bulletin> in the search field.  
Home Safe is a commitment to be vigilant about personal safety and the safety of co-workers. 
  Work Smart, Stay Safe

SYSTEM BULLETIN 
 
To: All Employees  US Date: April 21, 2025 
 
SUBJECT: Operations update: A message from Mark Redd. 
 
On April 28, we join people around the world in recognizing the International Day of Mourning. On this day, 
we remember and honour people who have been injured or lost their lives while performing their workplace 
duties. We also reflect on how we can make our workplaces safer. CPKC will host ceremonies in Calgary 
and Kansas City starting at 10:45 a.m. local time. Where it is safe to do so, whistles will sound in Canada 
and the U.S. at 11 a.m. local time. For more information on the in-person ceremonies, keep an eye on CPKC 
Station and CPKC XChange for details this week.  
  
Please take a moment on April 28 to reflect on those who have been impacted and how we can all contribute 
to a safer workplace. 
  
Nominate a unionized railroader for a 2025 Safety Award for Excellence  
If you know a unionized railroader who goes above and beyond when it comes to safety, recognize their 
commitment and actions by nominating them for a 2025 Safety Award for Excellence! It could be a fellow 
railroader who: 
• Goes the extra mile in their day-to-day work responsibilities to see that safety is always a top 
priority.  
• Continually sets a good safety example for their colleagues and the next generation of CPKC 
railroaders. 
• Is a mentor who introduced you to Home Safe when you first started at CPKC. 
  
Submit your nomination by clicking on the nomination form  on CPKC Station > Operations > Safety. 
Nominations close end of day Friday, May 9, 2025.   
  
Get ready for Day N

U.S., is less than two weeks away. It is very important that, if you are impacted, you take the necessary steps 
to ensure you are ready to operate within the CPKC systems.

guides in eBinder for assistance.

Department Pages > Operations > Operations Training Manuals, to access and familiarize yourself 
with all Day N support resources.

tracks. Of these injuries, 42 percent were serious. To reinforce the importance of safe work practices and 
compliance with CPKC’s procedures and standards, a safety blitz is underway and will run from April 14 to 
May 15.

Reference # CPKCSB-022-25                                    Posted Date/Time _____/_____/_____-________ 
 
SYSTEM BULLETIN 
 
To: All Operations Employees  US Date: April 24, 2025 
 
SUBJECT: International Day of Mourning – April 28, 2025 
 
On Monday, April 28, CPKC will honor International Day of Mourning. On this day, flags across the network will be 
lowered to half-mast and the company will observe a moment of silence followed by the sounding one long whistle 
salute to recognize the men and women who have been injured or lost their lives while on the job.  
 
At CPKC, never far from our minds are the memories of those who have died or have been injured at work while in 
service of the company.  
 
Moment of silence and sounding of whistle  
On Monday, April 28, at 1100 local time, employees are asked to observe a moment of silence. At 1101 local time, 
operating employees will sound one long whistle salute, if safe to do so. This is to remind us that everyone, no matter 
what their line of work, is responsible for safety in the workplace.  
 
Below are guidelines for observing the International Day of Mourning, in CPKC's various functional areas:  
 
Train & Engine Employees   
Where operationally feasible and safe to do so:    
• At 1100 local time, for those T&E employees not operating trains or performing transfer or engine 
movements, observe one minute of silence.   
• At 1101 local time, for those T&E employees operating trains or performing transfer or engine movements, 
sound one long whistle as a salute.   
• For T&E employees unable to observe one minute of silence at 1100, choose an appropriate time to 
recognize International Day of Mourning.   
 
Mechanical Employees   
Where operationally feasible and safe to do so: 
 
• At 1100 local time, observe one minute of silence.   
o Employees on the afternoon and evening shifts should stop and observe this one minute of silence 
at a time determined appropriate.   
o Employees working on the road are asked to safely park their vehicles and observe one minute of 
silence as close to the designated time (1100) as possible.   
• Following this tribute, safely resume operations.  
 
Engineering Employees   
Where operationally feasible and safe to do so, safely stop all track units and/or work equipment:   
 
• At 1100 local time, observe one minute of silence.   
o Employees working on the road are asked to safely park their vehicles and observe one minute of 
silence as close to the designated time (1100) as possible.   
o Crews unable to observe this designated one minute of silence should choose an appropriate time 
for their members to recognize International Day of Mourning.  
• At 1101 local time, sound warning alarms and/or horns as a salute.    
• Following this tribute, safely resume operations.
Reference # CPKCSB-022-25                                    Posted Date/Time _____/_____/_____-________ 
 
Intermodal Operations   
Where operationally feasible and safe to do so, safely stop all top lift machines and cranes ensuring no load is left 
suspended:   
• At 1100 local time, observe one minute silence.   
• At 1101, sound one long horn.   
• Following the tribute, safely resume operations.   
CPKC Offices 
If safe to do so, managers and/or supervisors at all CPKC offices and outlying work locations should arrange for 
their employees to:  
• At 1100 local time, observe one minute silence.  
• Employees on the afternoon and evening shifts will observe this one minute of silence at an appropriate 
time determined by local managers and/or supervisors.   
• Following this tribute, safely resume operations.  
 
Employees who are working from home or off duty are encouraged to pause for a minute of silence at 1100 local 
time to remember employees who have lost their lives or have suffered injury in occupational accidents . 
 
Home Safe is a commitment to be vigilant about personal safety and the safety of co-workers. 
 
 
Work Smart, Stay Safe

Reference # CPKCSB-024-25                                    Posted Date/Time _____/_____/_____-________ 
 
SYSTEM BULLETIN 
 
To: All Employees  US Date: May 5, 2025 
 
 
SUBJECT: Operations Update: A Message from Mark Redd 
 
 
On April 28, CPKC railroaders joined people around the world to honour fellow railroaders and 
other workers who have been injured or lost their lives while performing their workplace duties. 
The International Day of Mourning provides a very important opportunity for us to reflect on what 
we can all do to make our workplace safer so that we go Home Safe.  
 
With spring upon us, we must stay aware and ready to safely navigate hazards such as 
changing track conditions, flooding, storms, fire and conditions that can lead to slips, trips and 
falls. For more information about how to safely manage spring hazards, please read the 
Spring/Summer Hazard Awareness Education Package. Visit CPKC Station > Operations > 
Safety > Seasonal Bulletins.  
 
Day N systems cutover: Update 
I’m pleased to share that we successfully completed our inventory and systems cutover this past 
weekend, a significant milestone achieved through meticulous planning, teamwork and the 
unwavering dedication of our CPKC railroaders. I want to especially highlight and thank the 
railroaders who are embracing change with determination and stepping up to learn new 
applications and systems. Your adaptability and positive mindset are driving this transformation 
forward and are inspiring to all of us.  
 
With our technical cutover complete, we expect to see some issues with start up as employees 
are learning new systems and we see both technical and process issues that need to be fixed 
and/or updated. A 24/7 war room has been established to handle all urgent issues on the 
business and IT side. Specific issues that are currently high priority: 
 
• We are experiencing phone (IVR) issues with CMA. These are being worked on and 
there are workarounds to get ahold of the crew desk as this is being fixed. 
• Working through challenges with train build, inbound and outbound within the PTM 
application.  
 
It’s all hands on deck to ensure we are knocking down issues as they arise. We appreciate 
everyone’s patience and commitment as we work through this significant change together. Let’s 
keep building on this momentum and continue supporting one another as we progress through 
the next phases of our integration journey.
Reference # CPKCSB-024-25                                    Posted Date/Time _____/_____/_____-________ 
 
Nominations for 2025 Safety Awards for Excellence close May 9 
Nominations for this year’s Safety Awards for Excellence close this Friday. If you know a 
unionized railroader who embodies our Home Safe commitment and actions in everything they 
do, don’t miss this opportunity to recognize their efforts. Submit your nomination by clicking on 
the nomination form on CPKC Station. You can find the form by visiting CPKC Station > 
Operations > Safety.  
  
CPKC delivers strong Q1 results 
Last week, we announced first quarter results that once again reflect the strength of our 
railroaders and network. Despite the challenging extreme winter weather conditions we faced in 
the quarter, we delivered impressive results.  
 
During the first quarter, we achieved revenues of $3.8 billion, an increase of 8 percent 
compared to Q1 2024. Volumes, as measured by Revenue Ton Miles, increased 4 percent. Our 
reported operating ratio (OR) decreased to 65.3 percent from 67.4 percent in Q1 2024 and core 
adjusted combined OR improved 1.5 percent to 62.5 percent from 64 percent in Q1 2024. 
Reported diluted earnings per share (EPS) increased to $0.97 from $0.83 in Q1 2024 and core

eference # CPKCSB-25-25
  Posted Date / Time: ____/____/25 – ________ 
 
SYSTEM BULLETIN 
 
To: All Operations Employees All Regions  Date: April 30, 2025 
 
SUBJECT:  A message from the President & CEO: Strong Q1 results 
reflect the power and resilience of our railroaders and network 
 
Fellow railroaders, 
 
Today, we announced results for CPKC’s first quarter of 2025. Our world-class family of 
railroaders executed CPKC’s precision scheduled operating plan to safely and efficiently move 
solid freight demand to start 2025, producing strong first quarter results.  
 
During the first quarter, we achieved revenues of $3.8 billion, an increase of 8 percent 
compared to Q1 2024. Volumes, as measured by Revenue Ton Miles, increased 4 percent. Our 
reported operating ratio (OR) decreased to 65.3 percent from 67.4 percent in Q1 2024 and core 
adjusted combined OR improved 1.5 percent to 62.5 percent from 64 percent in Q1 2024. 
Reported diluted earnings per share (EPS) increased to $0.97 from $0.83 in Q1 2024 and core 
adjusted diluted EPS increased 14 percent to $1.06 from $0.93 in Q1 2024. These are 
impressive results, particularly given the challenging weather conditions we dealt with in the 
quarter. 
 
For more on the results, please see today’s press release on cpkcr.com.  
 
Key Milestones in Q1 
 
• CPKC and the Lanco Group/Mi-Jack sold the Panama Canal Railway Company to APM 
Terminals, a global terminal operator and an independent division of A.P. Moller - 
Maersk. The sale of this non-core asset creates value for our shareholders and reflects 
our commitment to optimize our assets as we focus on growing our core North American 
rail business through our unrivalled three-nation network.  
• On Feb. 6, we celebrated the official dedication of the Patrick J. Ottensmeyer 
International Railway Bridge. Completion of the additional span more than doubles our 
capacity to move freight through the border at Laredo, the largest international trade port 
of entry in North America. 
• In February, we announced our first share repurchase program since early 2021. This 
reflects our financial strength and progress in meeting our commitments to shareholders 
when they approved the CPKC combination.  
• San Luis Potosí was named 2025 Terminal of the Year as we celebrated our annual CEO 
Awards for Excellence. Brett Reynolds, a Track Maintenance Foreman in Swift Current, 
Sask., was named CPKC’s 2025 Railroader of the Year. Congratulations to all CEO 
Awards for Excellence winners!  
 
Safety 
 
In Q1, our Federal Railroad Administration (FRA)-reportable personal injury frequency 
decreased to 0.98 from 1.14 in Q1 2024 and our FRA-reportable train accident frequency 
decreased to 0.38 from 0.90 in Q1 2024.
R
eference # CPKCSB-25-25
I am very pleased with the notable improvements we achieved in our first quarter safety metrics. 
We can be proud of those results but must never be satisfied. The pursuit of safety excellence is 
a continuous journey at CPKC. Striving to go Home Safe every day with zero injuries and zero 
derailments is the standard of excellence we are pursuing. Keep your eye on the ball every 
minute of every day when it comes to operating safely and look out for your fellow railroaders.  
 
Staying focused, staying strong: Railroading in challenging times 
 
Over the course of history, railroads have continued to serve through instability and uncertainty. 
From two world wars to a pandemic, through good economic times and recessions, our railroad 
was there.  
 
Today, during these times of economic uncertainty, with our unique, unrivalled network that 
connects Canada, the United States and Mexico, the fundamentals of our success remain firmly 
in our control. The tremendous advantages of our unrivalled network remain the same today as 
they were on Day 1 two years ago. 
 
You, our world-class railroaders, embody the enduring relationship between these three 
countries, a bond that will stand the test of time.  
 
Our precision scheduling railroad model provides us with the playbook we need to serve our 
customers in the safest, most reliable and efficient manner possible. That model has enabled us 
to execute successfully and overcome headwinds – or take advantage of the benefit from 
tailwinds - time and time again.  
 
This moment in history must be no different.  
 
At CPKC, success means being laser focused on effectively executing the foundations of our 
business so we can provide the premium service our customers expect. It means controlling 
costs and maintaining industry-leading levels of safety. It requires us to maximize our assets 
and effectively lead our people.  
  
This is not a railroad built for one news cycle, one quarter or one political term. Ours is a forever 
story. The three great nations we serve remain more closely linked than ever and I believe those 
strong ties will remain. Trade flows and supply chains may see adjustments as trade 
relationships rebalance, but change means opportunity. 
  
We must not lose our focus or ease up on our fundamentals. Ever. How we perform is up to us. 
How we execute is up to us.   
  
The sense of pride I feel in this company – its people, its history and its future – remains 
unshakable. I appreciate the effort you make every day to deliver for our customers, our 
communities and, importantly, for each other. 
  
I am truly humbled to be railroading with you. 
 
Respectfully, 
 
 
Keith Creel 
President and CEO

This coming Monday, Americans will recognize Memorial Day, a day that honours U.S. service members

enjoying the long weekend that traditionally signals the  beginning of summer. I hope that our Canadian

Stephen Barber classroom at U.S. Operations Center 
On May 22, we will gather at the U.S. Operations Center to dedicate a classroom to the memory of Stephen 
Barber who, tragically, on February 19, 1999, was fatally injured in Kansas City while working at our

had just bought his first home. Together, let’s honour S teve by coming to work every day determined to 
look out for each other and do everything we can to go Home Safe.

increases, stay aware and report any issues you encounter. Exercise caution while operating locomotives 
to help minimize the risk of errant spark emissions, helping to keep our employees – and the communities 
in which we operate – safe.

for the TCRC and RCTC Collective Agreements that expired on December 31, 2023. We expect a decision 
within the next few days and will keep everyone posted once the Arbitrator renders his binding award.

impacts on the network. No two storms are alike, and you may have to make quick decisions when you 
encounter severe weather. Safety must be your priority when you encounter lightning, high winds, 
intense rain or tornadoes. Be aware of and practice the “flash to bang” measurement to track lightning 
distance; if the time between seeing the lightning strike and hearing thunder is 15 seconds or less, take 
shelter. Understand the difference between a tornado watch and warning and take steps to protect your 
safety in the event of a warning.  
 
It is also important that you take precautions when working in extreme heat and stay aware of the signs 
of heat stress, which can happen to anyone regardless of age or fitness level. Know and recognize the 
signs of heat stress so they can be addressed before becoming serious. Muscle cramping, headaches, 
weakness and dizziness are some of the signs. Make sure you drink water every 15-20 minutes, protect

SUBJECT: Employee Awareness - It’s Important to Stay Vigilant 
 
CPKC Public Safety Communications Center - 1-800-716-9132 
CPKCM KSOC - 011-52-82-8305-7911 
 
Dear Colleagues, 
CPKC is committed to providing a safe work environment. As employees, you are our eyes and ears on 
the ground and across the network. We count on you to keep a watchful eye during your day-to-day work. 
Because you can distinguish between suspicious activity and your everyday routine, we encourage you to 
be alert. If something does not look or feel right, report it. 
 
The CPKC Security Team is reminding employees to continue to do their part in protecting themselves 
and others by reporting suspicious items, persons, or activity. 
 
You can help us potentially identify suspicious activities by reporting any of the following situations: 
  
• If you observe anyone in a restricted or unauthorized area; 
• If someone quickly exits railway property once being noticed; 
• If someone becomes nervous or confrontational when questioned; 
• If someone is taking photographs or conducting surveillance/video recording; 
• If you see someone expressing an unusual level of interest in railway operations, such as: 
watching trains, inspecting railcars or track infrastructure, or attempting to obtain information; 
• If you notice anyone who does not have proper ID, uniform or personal protection equipment; 
• If someone attempts to conceal his or her identity; 
• If you observe the theft of speciality railway equipment/tools; 
• If an unauthorized person is testing security – by observing emergency response times or 
attempting to gain entry in restricted areas; 
• If you think someone might be attempting to impersonate a CPKC employee, through the theft or 
acquisition of uniforms;  
• If you notice someone who has possession of maps or drawings of railway infrastructure. 
  
CPKC Security and CPKC Police closely monitor world events at all times to assess potential risks to our 
company.  With your help, our awareness and ability to assess risks can be multiplied many times over. 
Safety is our collective responsibility, so it is important for all CP KC employees to remain vigilant and 
aware of the potential for suspicious activity on CPKC property. 
If you see something, please say something! 
 
Please contact the 
CPKC Public Safety Communications Center - 1-800-716-9132, 
CPKCM KSOC - 011-52-82-8305-7911, 
the RTC, Dispatcher, or your Supervisor

SUBJECT: Operations Update: A message from Mark Redd 
 
Family Days are great celebrations that bring railroaders and their families together across the network in Canada 
and the United States each summer. I hope you can join a Family Day event in your area! Events coming up in the 
next two weeks include: 
 
▪ Aug. 3: Mason City

▪ Aug. 16: Minot 
 
CPKC launches Southeast Mexico Express service  
 
Last week, CPKC and CSX announced that we have created a new rail transportation routing option across the 
southern U.S. with the Southeast Mexico Express (SMX), a new east-west Class 1 corridor that connects shippers in 
Mexico, Texas and the U.S. southeast. With Schneider as an anchor customer and the service providing faster transit 
times and better capacity for automotive, intermodal and carload customers, this new routing option is already 
delivering value and is another great example of the power of our unique network.  
  
New T&E resthouse opens in Toronto 
 
A new T&E resthouse opened in Toronto earlier this month. Officially completed July 1 with the first railroaders staying 
July 3, the resthouse has 12 rooms with cable TV and an attached bathroom with shower. It also offers a large 
kitchen, barbecue area, fitness facility and lounge so railroaders can connect and rest. Thanks to CPKC’s Facilities 
team for their ongoing work and commitment to creating modern, comfortable spaces for our frontline railroaders.  
 
Lord Strathcona visits Ogden headquarters in Calgary 
 
Last week, Donald Alexander Euan Howard, the 5th Baron Strathcona and Mount Royal, visited CPKC’s Ogden 
Campus, seeing first-hand the legacy today’s railroaders are building. Howard is a descendant of Donald Smith, the 
first Baron Strathcona and Mount Royal, whose financial support made completion of our railway in Canada possible. 
Smith famously drove the Last Spike Nov. 7, 1885, at Cra igellachie, B.C., completing the Canadian Pacific Railway 
and uniting a new country. During his visit, Lord Strathcona helped unveil the new Strathcona locomotive, CP 7470, 
which now bears the regimental logo of the Lord Strathcona’s Horse, a distinguished  Canadian armoured regiment.

CPKC will release our Q2 results on Wednesday, July 30. The following day, Mr. Creel will host a quarterly town hall 
at 0800 MDT. I encourage you to join the town hall if you can and hear more about how we performed in the second 
quarter and what’s ahead in the second half of 2025. Visit CPKC Station or CPKC XChange for details on how to join 
the July 31 CEO town hall.  
 
Stay healthy and stay safe, 
 
 
Mark Redd 
Executive Vice-President and Chief Operating Officer

To: All Employees  US Date: August 11, 2025 
 
 
SUBJECT: Operations Update: A message from Mark Redd 
 
Many locations across our network have experienced very high temperatures this summer. It is critical that you remain 
aware of the heat and your hydration levels during extreme hot weather. Take time to review the Spring Summer 
Hazard Awareness Education Package found on CPKC Station > Operations > Safety > Seasonal Bulletins. Some 
safety tips to remember when working in hot weather:  
 
• Drink a cup of cool water about every 15 to 20 minutes  
• Wear light and loose-fitting clothing  
• Use sunscreen  
• Take rest breaks in cooler or shaded areas  
• Know the signs of heat cramps, heat exhaustion and heat stroke  
 
Q2 Results and CEO town hall  
On July 30, CPKC released Q2 results that reflect your focus on delivering for each other, our customers and the 
supply chain that depends on the essential service we provide. We faced challenges in the quarter, from trade and 
economic uncertainty to issues in the south resulting from our systems integration, but you faced those challenges 
head-on, pulled together and delivered.   
 
In Q2 we made progress on personal injury rates, with Federal Railroad Administration (FRA) -reportable personal 
injury frequency decreasing to 0.77 from .84 in Q2 2024. This is great to see, and I urge you to keep up the good 
work! Our Q2 FRA -reportable train accident frequency increased to 0.97 from 0.70 in Q2 2024, serving as an 
important reminder to stay focused, stay aware and report track-related hazards. You can read more about the results 
in the Q2 CEO message on CPKC Station and CPKC XChange.   
 
At the July 31 Q2 CEO town hall, Mr. Creel spoke about the tenacity of CPKC railroaders, industry consolidation, 
how our network and team are unique and in a strong position and more. A summary of the town hall is available on 
CPKC Station and CPKC XChange and includes a link to listen to the discussion in its entirety.   
 
One team, many voices  
Approximately 20,000 railroaders power our network. Each of us is unique; our differences make us stronger both as 
individuals and as a team. A video was recently created to recognize our differences and unique contributions and 
encourage us all to celebrate each other and support an inclusive workplace. We are all railroaders! Watch the video 
on CPKC Station or CPKC XChange.   
 
2024 Sustainability Data Report  
The 2024 Sustainability Data Report was released last month, highlighting progress on our sustainability journey in 
our first full year as CPKC. Among our achievements was a 2.5 percent year-over-year reduction in locomotive 
greenhouse gas emissions intensity in 2024 thanks to investments in fuel -efficient technologies, increased use of 
biofuels and operational improvements. The report also underscores our commitment to industry-leading safety  
practices, building strong community connections, developing our people and operating as a sustainably driven 
company, all made possible through the dedication and hard work of CPKC railroaders across our three -nation 
network. I encourage you to take a moment to read the report on cpkcr.com > Sustainability.  
 
 Stay healthy and stay safe,  
 
Mark Redd 
Executive Vice-President and Chief Operating Officer

SUBJECT: Operations update: A message from Mark Redd 
 
We believe that every CPKC railroader is a leader, whether you lead people, lead by influence or lead by example. 
Every day we are presented with opportunities to lead with courage and intestinal fortitude, but it’s the challenges 
we face that truly test us and provide opportunities to grow and make an impact. It’s never easy, but we inevitably 
come out of these challenges better, stronger and more effective as individuals, teams and leaders. When we faced 
significant challenges in the Southern U.S. resulting from our systems consolidation in May, railroaders from across 
the network converged, coming together to help each other, teach each other and work through the issues. This 
was a tremendous example of tough inspiring leadership, and I want to sincerely thank every railroader who made 
a positive impact and got results. This is what good looks like! 
 
New hazard reporting process in U.S. 
All railroaders, regardless of role or title, play a part in our safety journey and are responsible for remaining vigilant 
and reporting incidents that occur on CPKC property. A new process is in place for reporting environmental and 
hazmat incidents that occur on CPKC property in the U.S.  
 
Most U.S. CPKC employees are impacted by this new process, except for Train & Engine crews that experience 
incidents while operating on the mainline. Those incidents will still be radio communicated to the U.S. Operations 
Center for handling. All other incidents that occur across the U.S. network, whether legacy CP or KCS, must now 
be reported to the Public Safety Communications Center by calling 1-800-716-9132. 
 
CPKC Women’s Open 
Last week, we held the 2025 CPKC Women’s Open at the Mississaugua Golf & Country Club in Mississauga, Ont. 
The tournament raised a record $4.5 million for cardiac healthcare in Ontario, with $4 million going to MacKids and 
the McMaster Children’s Hospital and $502,000 to Trillium Health Partners.  
Congratulations to CPKC Ambassador Brooke Henderson who claimed her second CPKC Women’s Open victory!  
 
The CPKC Women’s Open is the marquee event of our CPKC Has Heart community investment program, which 
aims to improve heart health in communities across North America. Since 2014, this event has helped raise more 
than $27 million in support of children’s cardiac research, equipment and care and the program overall has helped 
raise more than $60 million since it began in 2014.  
 
First co-located Americold warehouse opens in Kansas City 
On Aug. 12, a ribbon cutting marked the completion of the new Americold cold-storage facility located on CPKC’s 
property adjacent to our IFG Intermodal Terminal in Kansas City. The new facility continues the expansion of our 
North American cold chain solution with single line service stretching from Mexico City through Kansas City to Saint 
John, N.B.  
 
Stay healthy and stay safe, 
 
 
 
Mark Redd 
Executive Vice-President and Chief Operating Officer
